reason: The text demonstrates the Hebrew people actively and openly expressing their views and opinions. The passage contains multiple instances of public vocal expression: the people publicly acclaim the young king Joash with 'יְחִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ' (Long live the king!), they rejoice and blow trumpets ('וְכָל־ עַ֤ם הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ שָׂמֵ֔חַ וְתֹקֵ֖עַ בַּחֲצֹֽצְר֑וֹת'), and they collectively participate in destroying the Baal temple and its altars ('וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ כָל־ עַם֩ הָאָ֨רֶץ בֵּית־ הַבַּ֜עַל וַֽיִּתְּצֻ֗הוּ'). These passages explicitly show the people being not discouraged but rather fully engaged in expressing their political and religious preferences through vocal proclamation, public celebration, and collective action.
